chapters.title: By Nature and by Reason
chapters.source_excerpt: Section Two [6] We say, then: the necessity (wujūb) of the imamate and of the imams, peace be upon them, is grounded in natural disposition (jibla), innate constitution (fiṭra), nature (ṭabīʿa), intellect (ʿaql), governance (siyāsa), prescription (waḍʿa), and established norms (rusūm).13 It is obligatory in all revealed law (sharīʿa), religion, and religious communities, just as the existence of the Creator is…

chapters.title: Degrees of Excellence
chapters.source_excerpt: [15] The wisest among the philosophers speak of ten categories and hold that nothing can be mentioned or discussed except in relation to these ten: substance (jawhar), quantity (kammiyya), quality (kayfiyya), relation (idāfa), place (makān), time (zamān), possession (jidda), posture (nusba), action (fā'il), and affection (maf'ūl). The highest of the ten is substance, upon which all others rest and over which all…

chapters.title: The Ladder of Creation
chapters.source_excerpt: **Section Six** [23] As for fruit-bearing trees, the peak and summit among them is the date palm. It resembles human beings in having male and female, and it requires fertilisation just as animals require mating. Furthermore, every part of the date palm is beneficial and nothing goes to waste; its fruit is eaten at all times, whether raw or cooked. chapters.title: Governance and the First Principle
chapters.source_excerpt: [48] We also say that philosophers divided politics or governance (siyāsa) into three categories: governance of the individual (siyāsat al-khāṣṣa), governance of the family (siyāsat al-'āmma), and governance of the general public (siyāsat al-'āmma). chapters.title: The Imam in the Pillars of Faith
chapters.source_excerpt: [56] We also say that the ritual prayer — its arrangement, its prescribed standing, its direction toward the qibla, and the standing of the prayer leader (imam) at the head of the rows — constitutes a powerful indication of the imamate.
